title: 2014 Pymble Legal Studies Trial
notes: The source is scanned with no usable text layer. Section I (PDF pages 2–5) was rendered and read visually. No separate answer key was found; answers are reasoned guesses. No shared stimuli or figures occur in the multiple-choice section.

questions.stem: In which court would an appeal against a murder conviction be heard?

options.B: The Coroner’s Court
options.D: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal

questions.answerNote: An appeal against a Supreme Court murder conviction is heard by the NSW Court of Criminal Appeal.

questions.stem: Who has the burden of proof in a Local Court?

options.B: Defendant
options.D: Senior Counsel

questions.answerNote: The prosecution, represented in this context by the police prosecutor, bears the burden.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be considered an aggravating factor during sentencing?

options.A: Use of a weapon by the accused
options.B: Poor school attendance by the accused
options.C: History of mental illness of the accused
options.D: Minimal injury was caused to the victim

questions.answerNote: Use of a weapon increases the seriousness of the offence and aggravates sentence.

questions.stem: Which of the following human rights may best be described as a collective right?

options.B: The right to join a trade union
options.D: Voting rights

questions.answerNote: Environmental rights are commonly classified as collective or solidarity rights.

questions.stem: The use of anti-graffiti paint on the outside walls of a shopping centre is an example of which of the following?

options.B: Council regulation
options.D: Situational crime prevention

questions.answerNote: Hardening a target reduces opportunity and is situational crime prevention.

questions.stem: David decides to go to court instead of paying a speeding fine. What will happen next?

options.A: He will be charged with a driving offence.
options.B: He will be issued with a Court Attendance Notice.
options.C: He will be arrested and taken to the police station.
options.D: He will be remanded in custody until his case goes to court.

questions.answerNote: A person contesting a penalty notice is required to attend court by a Court Attendance Notice.

questions.stem: Alex and John have planned to rob a bank. On the way to the bank, the car breaks down. With what category of crime are they likely to be charged?

options.B: Summary offence
options.D: Economic offence

questions.answerNote: Planning an intended robbery can constitute a preliminary offence such as conspiracy or attempt.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a non-government organisation involved in the promotion and enforcement of human rights?

options.B: The European Union
options.D: The International Committee of the Red Cross

questions.answerNote: The International Committee of the Red Cross is a non-governmental humanitarian organisation.

questions.stem: 13-year-old Gerry has been found guilty of car theft. Which of the following is most likely to be a priority for the magistrate during sentencing?

options.B: Incapacitation
options.D: Retribution

questions.answerNote: Rehabilitation is a central sentencing priority for young offenders.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an argument in favour of the jury system?

options.A: It ensures a correct verdict in a criminal case.
options.B: It ensures a unanimous verdict in a criminal case.
options.C: It allows the community to participate in the sentencing process.
options.D: It allows the community to participate in the criminal trial process.

questions.answerNote: Jury service gives the community a role in criminal trials.

questions.stem: Ashley is initially charged with murder but in return for entering a guilty plea, she now faces the lesser charge of manslaughter. This is an example of which of the following?

options.B: Charge negotiation
options.D: Efficient use of police powers

questions.answerNote: A charge is reduced in exchange for a guilty plea, which is charge negotiation.

questions.stem: State sovereignty protects human rights by ensuring a nation state has the right to which of the following?

options.B: To elect to become a monarchy
options.D: To enact anti-discrimination legislation

questions.answerNote: Sovereignty lets a state legislate for rights protection (D); C (develop natural resources) is also a sovereign right but is not rights-protecting.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of bail?

options.A: To uphold the presumption of innocence
options.B: To uphold the rights of the victim
options.C: To allow time to prepare a defence
options.D: To allow time to gather evidence of innocence

questions.answerNote: Bail allows release pending trial and is consistent with the presumption of innocence.

questions.stem: Alice has been charged with the murder of her abusive and violent husband. Which of the following could she use as a defence to this charge?

options.B: Necessity
options.D: Automatism

questions.answerNote: On the question’s stated facts, provocation is the available partial defence most closely linked to the abusive relationship.

questions.stem: Despite signing the Convention on the Rights of the Child, a nation state fails to pass laws giving effect to this convention. This is an example of the effect of which of the following?

options.B: Political will
options.D: Operation of the United Nations

questions.answerNote: Treaty implementation in domestic law depends in part on the political will of the state.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a sentencing hearing?

options.A: To determine the penalty to be given to the convicted
options.B: To determine the penalties to be given to the accused
options.C: To establish the range of penalties to be given by the prosecutor
options.D: To establish that the accused has committed a punishable offence

questions.answerNote: A sentencing hearing determines the penalty after conviction.

questions.stem: John has been arrested and charged with a serious indictable offence. Which of the following statements is true about John?

options.A: The courts must grant him bail.
options.B: His trial must be held before a jury.
options.C: He has a right to test the evidence presented against him.
options.D: He has a guaranteed statutory right to a lawyer for his trial.

questions.answerNote: An accused has the right to challenge and test prosecution evidence.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of the media in the promotion and enforcement of human rights?

options.A: It encourages victims to take action.
options.B: It raises awareness of human rights issues.
options.C: It organises public demonstrations about human rights.
options.D: It ensures action is taken to remedy breaches of human rights.

questions.answerNote: The media’s main contribution is informing the public and raising awareness.

questions.stem: If the Police Commissioner was to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment, which of the following would need to be considered?

options.B: Security classification
options.D: Protective custody

questions.answerNote: A Police Commissioner would be at obvious risk from other inmates, so protective custody is the specific consideration; B (security classification) applies to every prisoner and is the other plausible answer. Preventative and continued detention are post-sentence regimes for high-risk offenders.

questions.stem: The conduct of criminal cases in NSW courts is subject to strict rules of evidence. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To ensure the prosecution case is strong
options.B: To ensure that the rights of the accused are upheld
options.C: To assist the judge in deciding on a sentence
options.D: To assist the jury in deciding the innocence or guilt of the accused

questions.answerNote: Rules of evidence help ensure a fair trial and protect the accused’s rights.
